seo_title: Edgar Allan Poe's Mysterious Final Days in Baltimore
fact_hook: Poe was found delirious in the streets of Baltimore wearing someone else's clothes.
fact_explanation: On October 3, 1849, Edgar Allan Poe was discovered wandering Baltimore’s streets in a state of semi-consciousness, dressed in clothes that were clearly not his own. He was admitted to Washington College Hospital, where he remained in a state of confusion and agitation until his death four days later. No one knows exactly how he ended up in that condition, and Poe himself was unable—or unwilling—to explain. Theories range from alcohol poisoning, to rabies, to a sinister case of cooping, a type of electoral kidnapping in which victims were forced to vote multiple times. Witnesses reported him calling out for unknown people and refusing to identify himself properly. His physical state included extreme pallor, delirium, and severe exhaustion, suggesting a combination of physical and mental trauma. Hospital records from the time are sparse, leaving historians with a tantalizing but frustratingly incomplete picture. Even Poe’s close friends had little insight, leading to decades of speculation. The clothing discrepancy alone fuels theories of abduction or foul play, rather than mere illness.
